messages:
Rafael Mendes: Need to lock the monitoring checklist for staged rollout of tiered batching defaults (flag ramp). Can we align here so on-call knows exactly what to watch + rollback signals?

Sean Gallagher: yup. I’d like this to be “copy/paste” into the rollout checklist doc. We should scope to beta: a few models/regions.

Allison Grant: +1. Also make sure we reference the *tier labels* so dashboards can be filtered (fast/standard/cost_efficient) and compare vs control.

Aisha Bello: I can draft the checklist items if folks confirm the metrics + thresholds. Biggest risk is tail latency from queue delay.

Sergio Costa: For dashboards: we have the new tiered panels landing in observability-pack, but some queries still WIP. I’ll paste what’s stable.

Logan Wright: Telemetry side: the new histograms are `rw_queue_delay_ms` and `rw_batch_size` with labels `model`, `region`, `route`, `tier`, `deployment_mode`. We should be explicit about which dimensions to slice on during canary.

Rafael Mendes: ok, checklist structure I’m thinking:
1) preflight (flag status, cohort)
2) canary stage 1 (1%)
3) canary stage 2 (10%)
4) ramp (25/50/100)
5) abort/rollback criteria

Sean Gallagher: Preflight should include “baseline window” (at least 24h for those routes) so we know normal variance. And confirm error budget burn for the tier is healthy.

Allison Grant: also confirm alert routing/ownership. If we page on tiered metrics it needs to go to runtime+SRE? Or SRE only with runtime as secondary.

Rafael Mendes: For beta we’ll page SRE primary, runtime secondary in #eng-runtime. (We can adjust for GA.)

Aisha Bello: Drafting. Metrics to watch (per tier + control):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end + stage breakdown (prefill/decode if available)
- Queue delay: p95/p99 `rw_queue_delay_ms`
- Timeout rate + cancellation rate (client cancellations)
- 5xx rate and specific error codes (overload/load-shed)
- Batch formation: `rw_batch_size` distribution (mean + p95) and `rw_batch_wait_ms`
- GPU util + memory pressure (OOM / KV cache eviction rate)
Anything else?

Sergio Costa: Add “streaming cadence” for streaming routes. We have `rw_stream_token_interval_ms` (p95). It’s noisy but catches the regression we saw.

Sean Gallagher: +1. For streaming, even if end-to-end p95 is ok, token cadence can get choppy.

Logan Wright: also watch “admission control / shed reason codes”: `rw_overload_shed_total{reason=...}`. If cost_efficient bumps queue delay too high you’ll see shed spike.

Rafael Mendes: Can someone propose concrete rollback thresholds? We need numbers, not vibes.

Allison Grant: Suggest tier-specific deltas vs control (same model/region/route):
- p95 latency: > +10% for fast/standard, > +20% for cost_efficient sustained 15m
- p99 latency: > +15% for fast/standard, > +25% for cost_efficient sustained 15m
- Error rate (5xx): +0.2% absolute sustained 5m (any tier)
- Timeout rate: +0.5% absolute sustained 5m (any tier)
- Queue delay p99: > 2x baseline for 10m (any tier)
These are “auto-rollback candidate” not immediate page for a single blip.

Sean Gallagher: For fast tier I’d tighten queue delay: if queue_delay_p95 > 15ms for >10m, rollback. Fast tier promise is low queueing.

Sergio Costa: Careful: some regions already sit at ~10–12ms p95 queue delay at peak. Maybe use “delta vs baseline” rather than absolute for queue delay.

Aisha Bello: ok: queue delay rollback as *delta*:
- fast: queue_delay_p95 > baseline + 10ms for 10m
- standard: baseline + 20ms
- cost_efficient: baseline + 40ms
Sound reasonable?

Rafael Mendes: Works for me. Also need “kill switch” criteria: if OOMs or crashloops increase, immediate rollback regardless of deltas.

Logan Wright: we can key off `container_oom_events_total` and `rw_kv_cache_evictions_total` (evictions won’t always be bad, but spike can indicate pressure). Maybe “OOM > 0 in canary pool” => rollback.

Chloe Martin: Console side: canary customers will look at “effective config” and complain if they can’t see tier in UI. But for SRE checklist, we should ensure we can correlate requests by flag variant. Is the flag injected as label?

Benji Okafor: Flag system adds `flag_tiered_batching_defaults=on|off` as a dimension in traces + metrics (not everywhere, but in the new runtime metrics yes). For rollout we should filter by both `tier` and `flag=on` to avoid mixing.

Allison Grant: Checklist should call this out explicitly: when comparing, use `flag=on` for canary and `flag=off` for control.

Sean Gallagher: Also add a “hold period” step: after each ramp step, hold 30–60m during peak traffic before moving. And do not ramp during incident / degraded region.

Aisha Bello: Draft checklist items (v0):
Preflight
- Confirm target cohort: model(s), region(s), route(s), deployment_mode(s)
- Confirm baseline window captured (24h) + peak times noted
- Confirm dashboards: Tiered Latency, Queue Delay, Batch Formation, Streaming Cadence, Errors/Timeouts, GPU/Memory
- Confirm alert routes + on-call coverage
- Confirm rollback owner (SRE) + runtime contact (secondary)

Stage 1: 1% canary (15–30m)
- Watch p95/p99 latency delta vs control
- Watch queue_delay delta vs baseline
- Watch 5xx/timeouts/cancels
- Watch stream_token_interval_ms p95 for streaming routes
- Watch OOM/crashloop + shed reasons

Stage 2: 10% canary (60m hold)
- Same checks + verify batch_size distribution moved as expected (sanity)

Stage 3+: 25%/50%/100% (hold at least 60m at each step; prefer peak)
- Same checks + check error budget burn rate

Rollback signals
- Any OOM in canary pool OR crashloop spike => immediate rollback
- p95/p99 deltas exceed thresholds (per Allison’s table) sustained 15m => rollback
- 5xx +0.2% abs sustained 5m OR timeouts +0.5% abs sustained 5m => rollback
- queue delay deltas exceed tier thresholds sustained 10m => rollback

Rafael Mendes: Looks good. Please add “post-change annotation” step: add deploy annotation + flag state so graphs are readable.

Sergio Costa: + link the dashboards. Here are the grafana URLs (staging-ish):
- Tiered latency: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rw-tier-latency
- Queue delay + batch: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rw-tier-queue-batch
- Streaming cadence: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rw-streaming-cadence
- GPU/mem: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rw-gpu-runtime

Allison Grant: add note: for Dedicated/Private, some metrics names differ. For beta we’re Hosted only, so ok, but don’t overpromise.

Benji Okafor: One more: rollback procedure should specify the exact flag + scope (model/region) so we don’t turn it off globally if only one model regresses.

Rafael Mendes: yup. Procedure: “set flag tiered_batching_defaults -> 0% for affected model+region; keep others unchanged; verify within 10m metrics normalize; open incident thread if not.”

Sean Gallagher: After rollback, require a short write-up: what signal triggered, which metric, attach graph screenshot link. Helps next ramp.

Aisha Bello: I’ll fold all this into the rollout checklist doc and post for review. :thumbsup: (ETA 30m)

Rafael Mendes: thanks all. Once posted, I’ll pin in #eng-sre and link from release brief.
